problem_type: Native tool protocol text mistaken for successful execution and unsupported document scope
symptom: DSML write_script text appears in chat without changing the creation document
direct_cause: The CLI emits assistant text rather than an MCP call; web document schema only supports cursor/selection/end while server accepts only append
class_root: Native completion and web tool exposure lack a binding to executable document operations and verified durable receipts
entry_points: runNativeAgent: OpenCode and Codex JSONL responses

external_sources.purpose: Native MCP remains the only executable tool transport; discovery is separate from model completion

invariants: Assistant text never executes tools and serialized call text cannot count as a successful native turn
Web document tool schema exposes only executable scopes; whole-document replacement requires a successful read
Write success contains a revision/hash verified against the persisted admitted document

door_reduction.why_not: ProductionHost must construct document ports and semantic tools separately; native events require their own CLI boundary. Read/type reference and construction are separate door-map entries.

generality_proof: Both native engines converge on runNativeAgent output validation. Both document write entries converge on persist and the admitted document identity; schema projection never fabricates browser selection.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Validate completed assistant text before publishing it
Expose supported web document scopes and require read before replacement
Verify durable document revision/hash before write receipt

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both engines buffer text and validate at process completion
Both persist via the same admitted document verification

recurrence.reason: Observed in two independent project transcripts; any model emitting textual call syntax reaches the same successful CLI exit path
same_class_scan: Inspected OpenCode and Codex text parsing and both document write consumers

prevention.invariant: Only native MCP execution can change project state; textual invocation output fails the native turn
prevention.failure_mode: Typed localized execution-incomplete error; no text parsing into side effects, no automatic retries
prevention.strategy: Validate completed native output, project web schemas to supported scopes, verify document save before returning success

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove unsupported browser scope exposure and unconditional text-event publishing; no fallback executor

dependency_lifecycle.target: Owner-supported runtime with successful real read/write/read acceptance on the deployed host
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No verified upstream fix for DSML text emission. Application validates outputs without vendor-specific execution fallbacks. Runtime updates alone cannot guarantee document persistence.
exit_criteria: When a newer owner-supported engine is installed, run the same real document read/write/read acceptance before changing runtime selection
Retain output validation across runtime upgrades

migration: No transcript or document migration. Existing conversations remain; prior DSML messages are never executed.
residual_risks: Underlying provider/native-runtime reason for textual DSML is not yet proven
Models may still decline or omit a tool without emitting protocol markers; prompts are not execution guarantees
Protocol-text detection intentionally covers responses starting with invocation markers; arbitrary natural-language claims or later quoted markup are not treated as executable intent.
